# How to Teach Claude a Repeat Task by Writing Down the Steps Once

> **In short:** You write the steps of a task you repeat in plain English, then ask Claude to turn them into a clear instruction you can reuse. Don't count on Claude remembering it between separate chats, so save the instruction text yourself and paste it in when you need it.

Do you write the same weekly update, sort the same email type, or plan the same kind of dinner every week? In this guide you'll turn that routine into a short, reusable instruction. By the end, you'll have a block of text you can paste at the start of a new Claude chat, so you don't re-explain the task every time. This is for anyone who repeats a task and would like a faster starting point.

## Before you start

- **A Claude account.** Sign in at claude.ai. A free account is enough for this guide, though heavier use may be limited on the free plan.
- **A notes app or document.** Your phone's notes app or a simple word processor works. You'll paste text between this and Claude.
- **One repeat task.** Choose something you do at least every week. Good first picks are a weekly recap, a standard reply to customers, or a meal plan.
- **About 20 to 30 minutes** for your first time through.

## Step 1 — Write the steps of one repeat task

Open your notes app and write out the task as if you were explaining it to a new coworker. Use short sentences and plain words. For example: "First I open last week's notes. Then I pull out three wins and two problems. Then I write a short paragraph for each. I keep it under 150 words." Include the small decisions too, like what tone you use or what you always leave out. Don't worry about making it neat; the goal is to get the steps out of your head and onto the page.

If your list feels too long, cut it to the five or six main actions. Claude can fill in details later, but it can't read your mind about the parts you skipped.

💬 Example: "Every Monday I write a team update. I read last week's notes, pick out three wins and two problems, write one short paragraph for each, and keep the whole thing under 150 words."

You'll know it worked when you have a short list of numbered or plain steps that someone else could follow without asking you questions.

## Step 2 — Ask Claude to turn your steps into an instruction

Open claude.ai and sign in. Look for the empty text box at the bottom of the screen where you type messages. Paste your steps into that box, then add a request asking Claude to organize them. Usually, you'll also see a send button, often an arrow icon, or you can press Enter on a computer keyboard.

Claude should reply within a few seconds with a formatted version of your steps. If the reply is a long essay or it skips your steps, don't worry. Just reply with "Please make it a numbered list of clear steps only." Asking for a specific format is one of the most reliable ways to get a useful answer.

💬 Example: "Here are the steps I follow for my weekly team update: [paste your steps here]. Please turn them into a clear, numbered instruction I can reuse. Keep the language simple and ask me one question if any step is unclear."

You'll know it worked when Claude's reply is a numbered list that matches the order of your original steps.

## Step 3 — Check the instruction and fix what's missing

Read Claude's version slowly, as if you were the one following it on a busy Monday. Does each step say exactly what to do? Are the limits clear, like "under 150 words"? If something is vague, type a correction in the same chat. For example, you might write that the paragraphs should start with the result, not the background. Claude will revise the list.

Also look for anything Claude added that you never meant. Sometimes an assistant adds a step like "check the facts with your manager" that doesn't fit your routine. You're the final editor, so delete or change anything that doesn't match how you actually work.

💬 Example: "Good start. Please change step 3 so each paragraph begins with the result, and remove the step about asking my manager for approval."

You'll know it worked when the instruction matches what you really do, and you could hand it to someone else with confidence.

## Step 4 — Save the final instruction where you can find it

When you're happy with the list, copy the whole thing. Paste it into your notes app, and give the note a clear name like "Weekly team update instructions." Keep it in one place you check often. This matters because Claude may not keep the instruction from one chat to the next, so the saved copy is your real reusable tool.

Some Claude setups offer a place to save instructions that apply to several chats, and the menu names for this can vary and may depend on your plan. Look for a settings or project-style area if you see one. If you don't see anything like that, the notes app works just as well, and you won't need to pay for anything.

💬 Example: Name your note "Weekly team update: Claude instruction" so you can find it in a few seconds next Monday.

You'll know it worked when you can open the saved note in under ten seconds and see the full instruction at the top.

## Step 5 — Start a new chat and paste the instruction

Next Monday, open claude.ai and start a fresh chat by looking for a new chat or new conversation button, often a plus or pencil icon. Copy your saved instruction and paste it into the text box. Then add this week's details, like the notes you want summarized. Send the message as you did in Step 2.

Claude's reply should follow the structure you saved. If it doesn't, paste the instruction again and add one sentence at the end: "Please follow these steps exactly." If it still drifts, the issue is usually a missing detail in your instruction, so go back to Step 3 and tighten it.

💬 Example: "Please follow these instructions exactly: [paste your saved instruction here]. Here are this week's notes: [paste this week's notes here]."

You'll know it worked when the reply has the same sections and length limit you wrote down, using this week's information.

## Step 6 — Adjust after a few uses

After you've used the instruction two or three times, make a small update. Note what Claude got right and what you had to fix each time. Maybe the paragraphs run long, or the tone is too formal. Edit your saved note with the better wording, so the next run starts from the improved version.

Keep the changes small. One or two fixes at a time makes it easier to see what helped. Over a few weeks, the instruction becomes a reliable starting point that saves you time.

💬 Example: "Last time the update ran over 150 words. Please add a rule that the total must stay under 150 words, and repeat that limit at the end."

You'll know it worked when your fourth or fifth run needs fewer corrections than your first one.

## Common mistakes

- **Expecting Claude to remember everything.** Separate chats may not carry over your instruction. Fix it by saving the text yourself in your notes app and pasting it at the start of each new chat.
- **Writing steps that are too vague.** "Write a good update" gives Claude little to work with. Fix it by adding specifics like word limits, order of sections, and the tone you want.
- **Accepting the first version without reading it.** Claude's first draft of your steps may add or change things. Fix it by reading every line and asking for changes in the same chat before you save.

## What this means for you

- **In everyday life:** Repeated personal tasks, like a weekly grocery plan or a monthly budget review, can become a saved instruction you reuse in minutes. Keep it simple, and update it when your routine changes.
- **For your business or work:** A recurring report, a standard client reply, or a meeting summary can be turned into a shared instruction your team can copy. Check that it fits your company's rules before sharing it, since Claude can only follow what you give it.
- **If you're just getting started:** Begin with one small task you already know by heart. The first instruction doesn't need to be perfect; you'll refine it each time you use it.

## Try it now

In the next two minutes, open your notes app and write three steps for a task you repeat this week. Then open claude.ai and paste them into the chat with this request: "Please turn these steps into a short numbered instruction I can reuse." You'll have your first reusable instruction before your coffee cools.
